resources.string: Shows each setting’s description on one line; a tap shows the rest, another folds it.
How the descriptions show when you come back to Settings.
Every description shows in full; a tap folds it.
Each description stays folded or unfolded as you left it.

Sleevesight reads what a player says it is playing (track, artist, album). It does not receive the audio or your other notifications. Android grants this with notification access. To find your music players, Sleevesight looks at apps that report what they play (playing or paused) and checks whether it is music (a track with a title and an artist); it stops checking an app for music once it has found some, until Sleevesight starts afresh (not each time you open it). A new player is added to this list switched off. Sleevesight does not follow a player that is off: it does not track what the player plays, and keeps or sends none of it.\n\nSwitch on the players you want Sleevesight to follow.
No players yet. A music app appears here, switched off, once you play music in it.

A player appears here, switched off, once it has played music on this phone while Sleevesight was running (whether in foreground or background).\n\nPlay a track in your player for a few seconds. Your player has to tell Android what it is playing, with at least a title and an artist. Most music apps do; most video apps do not.
Which players work: open the answer in your browser
Note dismissed. To show it again: Settings → Appearance → Restore dismissed messages.
Home lists only the players Sleevesight follows, not every player it has recognized.
External services providing information on artists and music

Sleevesight pulls information about the currently played music from services dedicated to music and from general information sources. Switch on the services you want Sleevesight to get information from.

Sleevesight uses LLMs to process, aggregate, and present information retrieved from sources. Use the settings to specify the model and effort; stronger models and higher effort provide better results at a higher cost. One service at a time. Switching off a service does not erase the most recently used model and effort settings.
Private API keys enabling external services
Share phone’s name with Type on a computer

Type on a computer lets you type an API key on a computer’s keyboard, sent to the phone over Bluetooth: tap the keyboard icon in a key’s field, with the page below open on the computer. Sharing the name lets the computer list the phone by its Bluetooth name while a session is open, instead of as “Unknown or Unsupported Device”; a name the phone cannot advertise is left out, and the session says so. Anyone nearby scanning for Bluetooth can see the name meanwhile.

Sleevesight uses external services that require authentication via API keys, obtained from each service’s own website. Your keys are stored encrypted on this phone, and each is sent only to its own service.
Sleevesight collects genre information from sources and compiles a short list of representative categories.
Sleevesight collects track, artist, and album information from sources and uses AI to generate readable descriptions based on the sourced evidence.
Listening history, kept on this phone

Sleevesight keeps information about the tracks you play on this phone (titles, artists, albums, and when they played), to avoid repeating itself within a listening session and to learn which track changes are your skips. Nothing of it leaves the phone.
Detailed information about the design, implementation, dependencies, licencing, and policies.
Internal settings, only in developer mode
Options for testing Sleevesight and reporting problems to the developer. This section shows only in developer mode.
An open music encyclopedia: recordings, releases, credits and release dates.

When MusicBrainz is busy, Sleevesight asks again, waiting longer each time, for up to this long before going on without it. A longer wait gives fuller genres and dates; a shorter one shows the insight sooner.

When your AI service is busy, the connection to it fails, or its reply breaks off, Sleevesight asks again, waiting longer each time, for up to %1$s before it shows the error. A longer wait fails less often; a shorter one tells you sooner.
When your AI service is busy or the connection fails, Sleevesight shows the error at once. A longer wait fails less often; a shorter one tells you sooner.
Articles on songs, albums and artists, and the facts behind them.
An open lyrics library: whether a song has lyrics, to tell sung tracks from instrumental ones.
Searches the web for articles about the track.

When a track is sung in a language other than English, also looks it up on Wikipedia and searches the web in that language. The insight translates what they give and says which citations it translated.
Looks up every track in English only.
Searches in the track’s language only when the English sources say little about the track itself. With Exa on, one more Exa API call for such a track.
Searches in the track’s language for every track that has one other than English. With Exa on, one more Exa API call for each such track.
Your %1$s key can no longer be read; see Secrets.
Your %1$s key can no longer be read.
When on, Sleevesight asks the sources below for genres of the track, its artists and its album, and shows them on the home screen. When off, no genre information is sought from any source.
Tags added freely by listeners, unmoderated; Sleevesight keeps those that name a genre.
Track changes with autowrite until saver is activated
Light or dark. The system’s follows your phone’s dark theme.
Shows a button beside Settings on Home that opens a menu of the light, dark and system themes.

Home shows a Lyrics button for the playing track, with links to its lyrics on the lyrics sites MusicBrainz links to, or, when it links to none, a search on Genius. A link opens in your browser; Sleevesight doesn’t show lyrics.
Search Genius when there is no link
How to use Sleevesight, every setting explained, and how it works and is made.
Sleevesight is free software: its code is on GitHub.

Under each insight, the grounding check’s counts in full: how many sentences are grounded, and how many come from the AI model’s own knowledge, are uncited, or cite missing evidence. Under Sources, the sources that are off too, which findings were kept from an earlier lookup or rejected, and the rejected matches.
A button on Home that collects what the app knows at that moment into a report, for you to review, edit and send from your mail app. Auto hides it while Home scrolls.
Hidden while the home screen scrolls, back when it stops.
Not shown; bring it back here.
How links are marked: a thin line below them, or a faint highlight behind them.
Outlines in teal, with a Developer tag, everything only developer mode shows, so your screenshots show what other users will not see.
Developer mode is on. Turn it off here to hide this section and turn off everything in it.
How Sources, the genres, and the song’s, the artist’s and the album’s insights open: in place on the home screen, as expandable boxes, or each on a page of its own, with a back arrow.
On a computer, or another device that has your keys, open the API keys page:
The following five words are a unique one-time secret, used to encrypt your API keys in a QR code. Only this phone can read keys from the code.
Provide these words to the QR generator page; the first three letters are enough. See instructions given there.
Use these words within %1$s. When expired, new words are generated automatically.
The phone forgets the words once you leave this screen.
Once done, tap Next to proceed.
Use your phone’s camera to scan the QR code provided by the QR code generator page. The phone will read the QR code and decrypt your API keys using the five words from step 1.
Once scanned, tap Next to proceed.

2. Point the camera at the code.
Any QR code that holds only this key works too.

Type the key on a computer’s keyboard instead of the phone’s. A page on the computer sends what you type to this phone over Bluetooth, encrypted, and it appears in the key’s field. The computer needs Bluetooth, and Chrome or Edge.

2. Read the QR code the page shows with the camera.

Purge keys removes every saved key from this phone’s storage, and deletes the key in the phone’s Android Keystore that encrypted them. Any copy left in the storage can then never be decrypted again (crypto-erasure). Sleevesight never sent your keys anywhere but to their own services, and never logged them. Purging keys from Sleevesight does not revoke them. You can still use your API keys elsewhere if you keep another copy.

The speaker button beside insights triggers your phone’s text-to-speech engine to read the text aloud. The engine is the one chosen in Android’s settings. Note: some, such as Google’s network voices, send the text to their server to be spoken.
When an insight is read aloud while music is playing, the app can temporarily lower the volume or pause the playback.
The music plays on, quieter, while the insight is read.
The music pauses while the insight is read, and plays on after it. A player that does not resume by itself stays paused.
Reading an insight aloud starts with the track’s title and artists.
Reads each new insight aloud as soon as it is written, while Sleevesight is on screen. Not while TalkBack or another screen reader is on, since it reads the screen itself.
When Dates, Genres or Lyrics has nothing from its sources, asks your AI service, searching the web as set under %1$s.\n\nEach question is a paid AI service call; with web search, also Exa API calls.

Lets your AI service search the web with Exa when it is asked, by a tap on Ask AI or automatically, and when it writes an insight the other sources fall short for: an artist they have nothing on, or a song they only list.
Your AI service answers from what its model learned in training, which can miss new or little-known songs. One paid AI call.
Sleevesight searches the web once with Exa and gives the pages it finds to your AI service, which answers from them. One Exa API call and one paid AI call.
